plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A long-lived herbaceous perennial with large, often fragrant, double or single blooms held above deep green, glossy foliage. It is a classic cottage garden favorite and a staple of cut-flower arrangements.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to China, Mongolia, and Siberia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens of North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and bloom for more than 50 years in the same spot, and ants are often seen on the buds feeding on sugary nectar, though they are not needed for blooming.

plants.name: Rosa canina
plants.description: A vigorous, arching deciduous shrub with delicate five-petaled flowers that appear along thorny stems. The blooms are followed by bright red rose hips in autumn that are rich in vitamin C.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to July)
plants.location: Hedgerows, woodland edges, and scrubland across Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia
plants.funFact: During World War II, British children collected rose hips from dog roses to make vitamin C-rich syrup when citrus imports were scarce.

plants.name: Iris sibirica
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with slender, grass-like leaves and graceful flowers on tall, slim stems. It thrives in moist soils and is valued for its hardiness and elegant, butterfly-like blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (late May to June)
plants.location: Native to central and eastern Europe and northern Asia; grown in meadows, wet grasslands, and gardens in cool temperate zones
plants.funFact: Unlike bearded irises that grow from rhizomes that need sun-baked drainage, Siberian irises prefer consistent moisture and can form huge clumps that go decades without division.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular subtropical tree that bursts into clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, often before the fern-like leaves fully emerge. Streets and parks turn violet when the trees reach peak bloom.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; planted in Mexico, California, Florida, the Mediterranean, and parts of Asia
plants.funFact: In Mexico City, the jacaranda bloom peaks in spring and the fallen purple flowers carpet the streets, and a local superstition says a blossom falling on your head brings good luck.
